entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
Mars Polar Lander was a robotic spacecraft lander launched by NASA on January 3, 1999, as part of the Mars Exploration Program. 

This lander was a crucial component of the Mars Polar Lander mission, aimed at studying the Martian geology and climate. 

The lander's primary objective was to investigate the Martian surface and subsurface, specifically the mid-latitudes, and to search for evidence of water and life. 

The Mars Polar Lander's legacy continues to influence our understanding of the Martian environment and the search for life beyond Earth.

The Mars Polar Lander's impact on the search for life on Mars can be seen in the subsequent Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity Rover) mission, which landed on the planet in 2012 and discovered evidence of ancient lakes and rivers.

Mars Polar Lander's failure to establish communication with Earth after landing on Mars serves as a poignant reminder of the risks and challenges involved in space exploration.
